name: Alexei Zhang
home: the blocks north of the port
life: “I still remember letting another worker receive a difficult supplier.” People around the window at Night Shift Donuts know Alexei by a small Thursday habit. Alexei knows when the going-home crowd and the coming-to-work crowd will both be there.
voice: I can start earlier if someone else receives the first delivery. I've been pretending to be indispensable there for years.
appearance: Alexei has a flat bridge to the nose and a mobile brow. Look for a soft fringe that falls across one eyebrow. On an ordinary day, the familiar outfit is a rust-colored canvas coat with a train token tied to a zipper pull. In conversation Alexei touches a knuckle to the chin when searching for a word.
personality: Alexei treats keeping somebody waiting as a serious discourtesy. This can turn a helpful person into an impatient one when everybody else needs a slower conversation.
agenda: To share the first supplier visit.
family: Frances Jimenez is Alexei’s younger cousin. Alexei is allowed to ask about the bad news afterward. Frances calls about good news first. Neither wants every family conversation to begin with a bill, a diagnosis or an apology. Asked about *Two left slippers*, Frances says, “I kept the wrong slipper as a joke until someone at the bus stop offered me its mate.”
connections: Patricia Keane. Sharing the first supplier visit protects a parent's last minutes at the school gate. Also in the story is Sylvia Kang (payroll colleague).
